note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Primary complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days, described as initially very watery, now very loose
  - Associated with vomiting ("throwing up everything," including fluids)
  - Sibling with similar symptoms; possible infectious exposure via household contact/school
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset 3 days ago
  - Symptoms ongoing, not improving; still frequent diarrhea (at least four times today), ongoing vomiting
  - Feverish sensation; subjective high temperature (not measured)
  - Abdominal pain located around the navel, described as sore and intermittent, worse with urge to pass stool
- ENT symptoms:
  - No throat swelling, throat closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia, odynophagia, drooling, nasal or ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, or facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling reported
  - No ear pain/hearing changes or neck pain/swelling reported
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No previous similar episodes; bowels typically normal (once daily)
  - No history of abdominal surgery or chronic abdominal issues
- Allergies and current medications:
  - No allergies mentioned
  - Current regular medication: vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Social context:
  - Lives with brother and mother
  - Working from home due to illness
  - Has tried oral rehydration salts (ORS)—salt and sugar mix from local source—three times a day for the past two days
  - Not able to keep food or fluids down

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling mentioned
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - No stridor, noisy breathing, or respiratory difficulty described
- Mental status and associated features:
  - No dizziness, syncope, or mental status changes reported
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Not recorded
- Presence of another person:
  - Lives with family; not stated if accompanied during consult

Assessment:
- No evidence of acute ENT pathology or allergic/anaphylactic signs
- Working diagnosis: Infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral (household/close contact exposure), with vomiting and dehydration risk
- Justification: Acute onset after exposure to sick contact; no ENT or airway involvement; ongoing GI symptoms and inability to tolerate oral intake

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Continue oral rehydration salts (ORS); advised on small, frequent sips to maximize absorption
  - Advised to take only simple foods if able (e.g., toast, biscuit); avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk
  - Sample of stool to be sent to clinic for analysis; urgent clinic appointment to be booked for hydration check and stool sample
- Instructions to patient:
  - If symptoms worsen (unable to tolerate oral fluids, increasing lethargy, reduced urine output, feeling more unwell), to attend A&E urgently
  - Call clinic back if condition deteriorates before scheduled appointment
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Worsening vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, reduced urination, or feeling significantly more unwell—attend emergency department (A&E)
- Follow-up:
  - Urgent clinic appointment for assessment and stool sample
  - No further ENT/allergy follow-up required based on current symptoms
  - No discussion of auto-injector, allergy or anaphylaxis care plan, or COVID-19 vaccine eligibility

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements for an acute ENT/allergy presentation:
  - Allergy history not fully documented
  - No history of prior anaphylactic reactions, emergency treatment, or auto-injector use stated
  - No explicit negative for airway or facial swelling beyond patient’s own history
  - Vitals and physical exam not included
● Internal conflicts:
  - None identified in the transcript
● Transcript quality:
  - Transcript clear, dialog uninterrupted; no significant technical or audibility issues
